headline: Revenue and profit surge on extra race, MotoGP consolidation
summary_short: Liberty Formula 1's Q1 2026 revenue jumped 59.1% y/y to $711M and operating income swung to $64M from a $67M loss a year ago, on one extra F1 race and MotoGP's first full comparable quarter since its July 2025 acquisition; both figures fell sharply q/q against Q4's seasonally heavier fee recognition.
summary_long: Revenue rose 59.1% y/y to $711M — three F1 races versus two, contractual fee escalation, and MotoGP's first full comparable quarter drove the gain — but fell 55.8% q/q against Q4's heavier season-based fee recognition. Operating income swung to $64M from a $67M loss, helped by the prior year's $50M one-time Concorde incentive payment and $11M MotoGP acquisition costs not recurring, partly offset by a $24M MotoGP operating loss. Constant-currency motorsport revenue growth was 12.5% versus 25.3% reported, reflecting a weaker dollar against the euro. Operating cash flow was $357M against $20M capex; cash rose to $1.33B. No shares were repurchased in the quarter; $1.1B remains authorized under the buyback program.

drivers.explanation: Revenue rose y/y on one additional F1 Event (3 vs 2), contractual fee escalation, and MotoGP's first full comparable quarter following its July 2025 acquisition.
Gross profit expansion is fully explained by revenue growing $264M against a smaller $118M rise in cost of motorsport revenue over the same quarter.
Formula 1 operating results improved and the prior-year period bore $11M of MotoGP acquisition costs plus a $50M Concorde incentive payment, partly offset by MotoGP's $24M operating loss.
Consolidated Adjusted OIBDA rose $108M y/y, primarily from higher Formula 1 Adjusted OIBDA and the MotoGP acquisition.
The 2026 F1 calendar was cut to 22 events from 24 after Bahrain and Saudi Arabia's April races were called off due to the Middle East conflict, reducing future event-linked revenue.
